coordinates.locator: MapCERN building layer, building 888 (EHN2): centroid of the building outline returned by the CERN GIS service (query for buildings 887 and 888, outSR=4326)
coordinates.note: Campus-grade point: the centroid of the EHN2 building outline in CERN's own GIS layer (about 95 m across). The COMPASS/AMBER spectrometer stands inside the hall at an offset that no fetched source publishes; the point is not a surveyed detector position.

name: EHN2, CERN North Area (Prévessin)
notes: EHN1 (building 887) is the neighbouring hall; the existing site:cern-neutrino-platform-ehn1 carries a coarser campus point for it.
COMPASS is placed here on the strength of the AMBER letter of intent ("the existing spectrometer in EHN2"), which describes the COMPASS spectrometer being reused.

summary.plain: Experimental Hall North 2, a large surface hall in CERN's North Area at Prévessin in France, where the COMPASS and AMBER spectrometers on the M2 beam line study the structure of protons and other hadrons.
summary.technical: EHN2 (CERN building 888) in the SPS North Area, Prévessin site: hall of the M2 muon/hadron beam line hosting the COMPASS spectrometer (2002-2022) and its successor AMBER; the point is the centroid of the building outline in CERN's MapCERN GIS layer.
